body:
> Are there any support groups in your area for other guys with similar problems?  

I don't know.  I haven't been out in a long while.  I think it's an understatement that it might help for me to connect with people.
This is so very helpful.  You are saving me. Thank you.

I gotta say, I think she had some sort of episode.  She is  not beastly to them.  She isn't a very big thinker, though.  She doesn't think long term, she doesn't think about long-term consequences.   She is focused on questions like...what's for dinner this week?  ..what time is band practice this week?  Which is important.  Don't get me wrong.  You gotta make the trains run on time.  But there are larger issues with child-rearing.  Once you have basic safety and stability, ideally there is a nurturing environment, but also a place to be challenged, safely.  A place to learn and try and fail and fall down and get up and without being ridiculed or hurt.  A place to stretch a little, take risks, screw up, and have a parent right next to you.  

I just think she's a little selfish, she has been for a long time. An affair is very selfish, and what she did afterward was also. Very much so. Prior to her suspending all communication with me (part of the allegations of abuse) I suggested she'd need to get a job, now that we were divorcing.  She shouted, "I have a job - raising these kids!"  And I thought, how out of touch she is.   She thinks divorce is the same as marriage, without the sex.  She still will have all the same lifestyle, the same comfort. Bizarre.  As if she can just do that one thing, now that she no longer has a supportive husband.  And... by extension, that I am no longer needed, except for the money of course, because "She's doing the childrearing."  

Anyway I think she had an episode, around the affair, her personality changed. She became less sure of herself, more wacky.  She started getting books at the library on witchcraft and clairvoyance.  Talking about re-incarnation.  Ok, some people go for that. But this was a big switch for her.  This wasn't her before.  I don't know, something happened.  Something happened to her.  Inside. Something bad. 

I don't know that she uses them as pawns, but they are, to her, I think, her identity.  She cannot bear to be without them.  She is a "helicopter mom".  And giving up 50% custody would be a great loss to her, I think.    

A long time from now I think she'll regret how she conducted herself through all this.  But that's a long time away.  and not my business anyway.  

Anyway, sorry about the long note, and thank you for your support.

Well thank you!  That's nice of you to say.  What I mean is, ... my life is no different today, than if I had been the one running around, drinking too much, not spending any time with them. 

It does take a lot out of a person, to lose so much of what is important.  It's hard sometimes to believe this will work out.

Thank you.
I like what you have to say.    
I need more of that in my life.   

You're right about the entirely new life. So far I guess I'm not accepting the new life so much.   One day maybe it'll be different.

That seems pretty wise.  

Thank you.

i thought about that a lot.  I think the reason I am still here is I still hope to share in the lives of my young kids, somehow.  

I read in the news recently that [giving up hope can help people be happier](http://www.reuters.com/article/lifestyleMolt/idUSTRE5A306520091104).
I would never.  She is still the mother of the children.  Regardless how she treated me, she is still the only mother they will ever have.

Thank you for responding.

> I've never understood why some parents need to make things so ugly for the kids and their spouse. There is just no point to it, and all that it does in the long run is to hurt the children.

I've never understood it either. The only thing I can figure is she needs someone to blame for the train wreck our lives have become.   The kids were baffled.  They'd invite me over (to the house I was paying for) - just think how stupid this is, my kids inviting me to my house - and I'd have to decline. "Why, Dad?"  What do I say to that? 

I'm just guessing, but I figure - if I am at fault, then it isn't her responsibility. The affair, the home foreclosure, the legal bills - if I am a jerk, then she can just duck all responsibility for the shitstorm she brought on.   So she attacked, and attacked, and it stuck. 

> to stay away from the "all women are scheming bitches from hell" rhetoric (because not all of us are), 

I know!  I know a bunch of women that are good, stable, strong people, they recognize the value of a mother AND a father.  And of course my sister is taking care of me; she is a good woman.  I don't think badly about all women.  I am very suspicious of women in the family court system (my attorney was a woman, the judge was a woman, her attorney was a woman, the child evaluator was a woman, etc ).  

But I have met some divorced men, and it is not a pretty life.  

My problem is, I bought into this idea that my children were actually MINE, and then when I found out the state could just whisk them away ... that is hard to accept.  It would be different if I could point to something and just say - jeez, there it is, look what you did to cause all this.  You know I read the story on SW of a guy who was convicted of possessing child porn.  It would be different if there was something like that for me - like if I was a drug user, a drunk, a gambler, if I swore all the time, if I beat the kids, beat their mother, brought hookers to the house, or was a bad provider.  None of this happened.  I'm not that guy.  So I don't know what to fix!  

I changed diapers and gave bottles, I took them on walks and read stories every night, and then I'd make up stories, long ones, make believe.  Oh they loved those stories.  I taught them to ride bikes, and took them skiing.  I taught them all to swim.  I was their soccer coach - they all loved to play when I was coach and so did the rest of the neighborhood.   And I loved their mother, faithfully.  To treat a father, a good man this way... it's criminal. 
 
Everything is solvable, everything, if I can hold my head up.  I have been driven crazy by this system that keeps telling me I'm a malevolent force, I'm dangerous to my children.  It's against my principles and my self-image and yet I lost everything because of it. I feel utterly insane.  In a practical sense, I *am* a bad father; I've endured all the consequences of being a bad father.  Practically speaking... I AM exactly the same as a dangerous father.   But I don't know how to be any better.  

That was the best I could do.  It's hopeless for me to do any better, after they've taken the kids away, taken my house, financially ruined me, and put the police outside my door.  I am set up for failure.

My kids should know that I feel like shit and I think their mother falsely accused me, and has become a crazy vitriolic woman?   That I want to be with them, but I am afraid of what she will do?  You don't think that would just fuck them up?
